The regular seats have a few stowage options, including a small compartment next to the seatback with a mirror where you can tuck in provided noise-canceling headsets and amenity kits. There is another small compartment with a water bottle holder in the aisle-side armrest that can be raised or lowered up to 11 inches. As I mentioned, these seats have doors that will eventually close, and I measured them at 54 inches from the top to the floor. The gap between the armrest and the preceding seat shell is 9 inches. So, it can be a tight squeeze, but it's pretty standard. The ledge next to the seat on this side has a glossy faux-marble shelf and a wireless charging pad for phones that juiced my iPhone 17 Pro by about 1% every five minutes. Next to that is a corded remote for the entertainment system. Beneath this shelf and labeled with helpful icons, there is a universal power plug and two USB-C ports (so if you have older devices, you might need to bring a USB-C to A converter). Now for the fun part: In addition to buttons for preset seating positions, you could control the individual components of the seat using a touchscreen pad near the armrest. It took me a while to get the hang of it since it's sort of like a scrolling scale, but it was fun to use. This pad could also control the lights and even change the color palette to suit your mood. I spent way too much time playing with that feature. The seat's 19-inch OLED 4K entertainment system is also a touchscreen, and the massive tray table deploys from below that. It can be unfolded to a whopping 24-by-16-inch surface with plenty of space for a meal service tray and my MacBook Air at the same time. When it came time to rest, I reclined the seat to its full 78-inch lie-flat length, which was plenty long for me but might not be quite enough for taller travelers. The foot cubby is 12 inches tall and 16 inches wide at its opening, so that was enough space for me to roll over from one side to the other without knocking my toes; however, if you have really large feet, you might feel constrained. Business-class passengers share four lavatories (one per 16 passengers). Two are behind the flight deck near the front galley, and the other two are by the second galley. Given the length of this flight, they only really got busy just after meal service, and the crew did their best to keep them clean. There was a mix of Perricone MD and Therabody products included. Finally, I appreciated the overhead air nozzles, as they kept my seat cool when the cabin was otherwise a little too warm for me. Most passengers were also considerate and kept their windows' electronic shades set to the darkest mode for most of the flight so that everyone could rest. Amenities in United's Elevated Polaris business class These may be new seats, but passengers will still find the airline's signature (and beloved) Saks Fifth Avenue bedding on board. Each seat came stocked with a bedding set that included a firm cooling gel pillow for lumbar support, a soft medium-size pillow, a lightweight blanket that I used as a seat pad and a more substantial duvet wrapped in plastic. The only thing I would have preferred is for the larger pillow to also have a wrap so I could stow it until I needed it. I just kept it down in the seat rather than try to stick it in the overhead, though, so I could keep it clean. I also found a pair of soft slippers on the seat's ottoman and donned them for most of the flight rather than wearing my own shoes. There was a colorful blue-striped Brooks Brothers amenity kit stocked with the following products, including skincare items from Perricone MD: - A toothbrush and toothpaste - Ear plugs - Eye mask - Socks - Tissues - Pen - Perricone MD Vitamin C cleansing wipe - Perricone MD Vitamin C eye gel - Perricone MD Vitamin C hand cream - Perricone MD Vitamin C face mist - Perricone MD Vitamin C lip balm The inclusions were nice, and I actually appreciated how compact the kit itself was, making it easy to stow in the seat-side compartment. The entertainment system felt very advanced. It was a 19-inch HD screen with accessibility options, and it was very easy to navigate. Luckily, it also had Bluetooth capability, so I could connect my own earbuds when the seat's headphone jack was not working properly. (Apparently, this has been a widely reported issue.) Once I did connect, though, the sound was good, and I appreciated the selection of movies and TV shows. Among the new releases were "The Devil Wears Prada 2," "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie" and "Project Hail Mary." The television shows included selections from HBO, including "House of the Dragon" and "Rooster." United is currently rolling out Starlink Wi-Fi, which is free to MileagePlus members on equipped planes. Unfortunately, this Dreamliner wasn't one of them. MileagePlus members could select a free messaging plan for phones that worked well enough on my iPhone for texting and WhatsApp, but not for email or any other apps. Instead, I sprung for the full-flight paid Wi-Fi plan, which was available for a mere $8. It was sufficient for email and some light browsing, and it was easy to swap service between my laptop and phone. How was the food in United's Elevated Polaris business class? After most of the business-class cabin boarded, flight attendants came by offering a choice of water or Gambino prosecco, which retails for about $10. I stuck to water since United has recently upgraded its inflight wines, and I was waiting for the good stuff. The airline allows you to preorder your meals in business class up to 24 hours in advance, and there was one main course choice of salmon available exclusively for preorder. I ordered one of the other dishes in advance to be sure they would have it. Service began about 20 minutes into the flight with a choice of beverages and a little ramekin of warmed nuts. About 20 minutes and another beverage service after that, the staff brought out the first course, which included a choice of: - Spiced seared prawns with chorizo dukkah and cauliflower puree - Mozzarella with charred grapes and balsamic vinegar cream - Baby greens salad with cherry tomatoes, Parmesan and marinated artichoke hearts They served entrees about an hour into the flight. Options included: - Beef tenderloin with rosemary Parmesan Hasselback potatoes, ratatouille and demi-glace - Frenched bone-in chicken breast with creamy polenta, broccolini and caramelized onion demi-glace - Orechiette pasta with white fava bean puree, sundried tomatoes and sauteed mixed vegetables - Seared salmon with braised lentils, asparagus and lemon-thyme butter (the preorder option) I had the beef, and while the piece of meat was well-cooked, the potato that came with it was more like a plain baked potato; the ratatouille was mainly chopped bell peppers in the semi-sweet demi-glace sauce, so I mostly scraped that off. For dessert, there was a choice of: - Made-to-order ice cream sundaes - Lemon pound cake - Cheese plate with fresh fruit I couldn't resist the sundae with the works, and the flight attendant assigned to my row made it expertly. Among the wines on offer were: - Laurent-Perrier La Cuvee Brut Champagne - Stony Hill SHV chardonnay from Napa Valley, California - Chateau Guiraud G Bordeaux Blanc from France - Whispering Angel Rosé from France - Shafer One Point Five cabernet sauvignon from Napa Valley - Lingua Franca Avni pinot noir from Oregon - Taylor Fladgate Late Bottled Vintage Port There was also a variety of sodas, juices, Illy coffee, Twinings teas and beers like Michelob Ultra, Stella Artois and Bell's Two Hearted IPA. As you can see, United has really stepped up its wine game with that Champagne and the cabernet sauvignon, in particular, which retails for well over $100 a bottle. It tasted great in the air, too. Between meals, there were oranges, bananas and potato chips in the galley, and you could also request instant noodle soup. However, the most interesting meal choice was actually the light option, which you could order up to two hours before arrival. It was dubbed a "Tapas" selection and included up to four of the following dishes to mix and match: - Hainan chicken and rice with bok choy and carrots, inspired by Singapore's Maxwell Hawker Centre - Vegetarian curry puff - Laksa with noodles, prawns, fish cake, hard-boiled egg and sambal - Soba noodles with goma dressing, chili oil, edamame and enoki mushrooms I ordered one of each, and the flight attendant came back with the tray around three minutes later. Honestly, I should have just had this as my main meal since the dishes were light, fresh and flavorful, providing a little taste of Singapore. After that meal, I snoozed a little longer and then worked for a few hours. About 90 minutes before arrival, the crew turned on the cabin lights and began serving a prearrival meal. The choice of main dishes included: - Poached shrimp with chicken broth congee, ginger and scallions - Chive scrambled eggs with chicken sausage, potato rosti and roasted tomatoes - Ricotta pancakes with caramelized banana, honeycomb butter and toasted walnuts I had the poached shrimp in congee, and the ginger and scallions lent the dish some much-needed flavor. The tray also came with a bowl of fresh fruit and a croissant. All the meal services were efficient and well-executed. I would rethink my main meal order, and perhaps just go for the tapas course since it was much tastier and more interesting than the two regular meal services. If it's available on your flight, I recommend trying that. One piece of advice: If you're interested in what's on the food and beverage menu for your flight, you can check your flight's status on the United website, click on the button for "inflight menu" and select your class of service to see the options listed. Would you recommend United's Elevated Polaris business class? United's new Elevated Polaris business class is an exciting new option for flyers on the airline's long-haul routes. Hopefully, award availability will continue to be good as more freshly delivered Dreamliners with the new seats on board come online. I also hope to fly the seats again to try out the roomier Studios and to test out whether closing doors improve the experience. For now, though, the new Polaris product is a great way to fly from San Francisco to both Singapore and London, and I'll be on the lookout for more opportunities to try it out. Related reading:

item.title: A New York City foodie's secret to saving on restaurants? Blackbird's dining loyalty program
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.54
A New York City foodie's secret to saving on restaurants? Blackbird's dining loyalty program New York City has some of the best independent restaurants and coffee shops in the world. It's one of the reasons why I love living here, but it also means dining is easily my largest expense outside of rent each month — and most dining loyalty programs that help you save money at the places you eat at regularly are centered around national chains. Enter Blackbird. Blackbird is a loyalty program and payment app designed for independent restaurants and cafes. A friend introduced me to it earlier this year, and I've since fallen in love with it. You can earn and redeem rewards, access special perks, split and pay your bill and more via the app. The program even has elite status tiers that offer more value. For anyone unfamiliar, I'm breaking down all the program's pros and cons to help you decide if it's worth investing your time and energy. Why Blackbird is a game changer for big-city dining Blackbird allows you to earn Fly rewards points at member restaurants when you check in via the app. The more you check in and spend, the more valuable each visit becomes thanks to the program's loyalty tiers. Those just joining will earn 3 Fly points per dollar spent, but you can earn up to 7 Fly points per dollar spent at the highest Blackbird Club loyalty tier. Right now, Blackbird is available in nine destinations: - New York City (including all boroughs, plus Jersey City and Hoboken, New Jersey) - The Hamptons, New York - Charleston, South Carolina - Los Angeles - San Francisco - Denver - Aspen, Colorado - Vail, Colorado - Breckenridge, Colorado The list of participating restaurants is still growing, but there's a solid number of available spots in New York City currently — from easy weeknight dinner spots like Barn Joo to chains like Tacombi to cocktail bars like The Tusk Bar. I also took a look at available options in Blackbird's other locations. Understandably, New York City has the largest concentration of participating restaurants, but the other major cities on the list have a decent selection of restaurants, too. Checking in is as easy as tapping your phone to the small black Blackbird puck at the host stand, and it's easy to pay your bill (or split it among friends) directly in the app. The best part? You can even stack rewards with your credit card to double up on earning. For example, if you use your American Express® Gold Card to pay your bill through Blackbird, you'll earn Fly points and 4 American Express Membership Rewards points per dollar spent (on up to $50,000 per calendar year, then 1 point per dollar). Related: Best credit cards for dining Blackbird Club tiers If you spend enough with Blackbird throughout the year, you'll get access to higher earning rates and additional benefits via the tiered loyalty program. You get access to higher tiers of the program by spending with Blackbird Pay or preloading money into your Blackbird account to use at checkout (similar to how you can preload money into your Starbucks Rewards account). Here's a quick breakdown of each tier: | Elite status tier | How to qualify | Earning rates | Key benefits | |---|---|---|---| | Member | Spend $500 in a calendar year, or preload $250 to your Blackbird account. | | N/A | | Regular | Spend $5,000 in a calendar year, or preload $2,500 to your Blackbird account. | | | | Friends & Family | Spend $10,000 in a calendar year, or preload $5,000 to your Blackbird account. | | | I wouldn't recommend preloading money into Blackbird to hit any of the elite tiers, as that would limit your ability to double-dip with credit card rewards when paying the bill at the restaurant, but if you do spend enough at Blackbird restaurants throughout the year to gain access to elevated earning rates, priority reservations and concierge help, those are all potentially valuable benefits. The value breakdown Earning and redeeming with Blackbird is surprisingly straightforward. Depending on your status level, you'll earn between 3 and 7 Fly points per dollar spent, and 100 Fly points equals $1 in spending power toward future Blackbird purchases. That means that even at the free level, you're getting a 3% return on spending, which is on par with a lot of credit card earning rates (and remember, you can also earn credit card points or miles on top of your Blackbird earnings). At the highest member tier, you'll get an impressive 7% return on spending. Blackbird also offers opt-in challenges that let you earn additional Fly points (including a first-time user challenge) and a referral bonus, making it really easy to get immediate value from the program even after just one purchase. A concrete example: I spent $45.30 at a Mexican-focused Tacombi location for my first-ever check-in and got 4,095 points total (3 points per dollar spent on the bill, plus a referral bonus and a first-time bonus). Given that points are worth 1 cent each, I had nearly $41 to spend on a future Blackbird Pay bill. The downsides of Blackbird I have laid out many of the pros in this article already, but there are also some downsides to consider. Only nine destinations are currently participating, and within each, only select restaurants are available. In New York City and the other major participating metropolitan areas, like San Francisco and Los Angeles, you'll have plenty of options where you can earn rewards, but even in the Big Apple, the reality is that the majority of restaurants in the city aren't currently on Blackbird. In the Colorado mountain towns where Blackbird operates (Vail, Breckenridge and Aspen), your options for Blackbird are fairly limited. Another con is that the bill split feature doesn't allow you to itemize. If your friend group tends to share food or split things evenly regardless of itemization, that's not an issue. But if you want to itemize, you'll have to do it the old-fashion way: Pick one person to get the full tab, calculate each person's share separately and then settle via Venmo or Cash App. Who will find Blackbird most valuable? Blackbird has the potential to be a really valuable program — but only for the right user. Consider joining if you're: - A foodie who lives where Blackbird operates. Until Blackbird adds more cities, this program is only valuable to those who eat out often in the nine destinations where Blackbird is currently available. - Someone who often eats family-style meals and splits the bill with friends. The ability to split the bill directly in the app is a great benefit for friend groups like mine, where everyone wants to earn credit card points and miles on the meal. We tend to split things evenly instead of itemizing, so it works perfectly for us. - Regularly spending at least $500 on dining a year. Spending $500 per year will get you Member status and an elevated 4 points per dollar spent earning rate. If you also happen to have the Amex Gold, which offers 4 points per dollar spent on dining worldwide (on up to $50,000 per calendar year, then 1 point per dollar), you'll earn a total of 8 points per dollar spent on every qualifying meal. - An adventurous eater who likes trying a variety of restaurants. With Blackbird, you don't have to commit to being loyal to a single restaurant or chain to earn or redeem rewards. Bottom line I love a good travel redemption as much as the next girl, but there's something to be said about an easy way to earn rewards and benefits on an everyday expense like dining. Blackbird is straightforward to use, earns valuable rewards at an array of restaurants and allows me to stack rewards with my credit cards of choice. That's a no-brainer for someone like me who lives in an expensive city like New York and dines out at least once a week with friends. Know, though, that we've seen this movie before with loyalty programs that offer huge sign-up incentives and high earnings without fees. In some ways, this program feels a little too good to be true to me, and, usually, that means it is too good to be true in the long term. (Looking at you, MoviePass.) Still, the current earnings are simply too impressive to ignore, so I'm going to make the most of this program while its points are valuable and its earning rates are high, no matter which status I hold. If you sign up for the program, I'd recommend you do the same. TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: Better stays and bigger value with the Marriott Bonvoy American Express cards
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.50
Better stays and bigger value with the Marriott Bonvoy American Express cards There's a reason TPG awarded Marriott Bonvoy with Best Hotel Loyalty Program for two years and counting. Actually, there are several. With more than 30 brands and over 9,000 properties across the globe, you'll find exactly what you are looking for when you stay with Marriott, whether it's a luxury stay, a budget-friendly getaway or anything in between. When it comes to earning and redeeming points, Marriott Bonvoy's structure is surprisingly simple and lucrative. Marriott Bonvoy members earn up to 10 points per dollar spent on qualifying charges at hotels participating in Marriott Bonvoy, which can be redeemed for hotel stays and room upgrades, or transferred to more than 38 airline programs. And the perks you can get at Marriott Bonvoy's elite status tiers — like bonus points, space-available room upgrades, early check-in and late checkout (subject to availability) — add comfort and value to your stays when booked with a qualifying rate at hotels that participate in Marriott Bonvoy. Room upgrades are subject to availability upon check-in and only available to Gold and Platinum Elite members. Right now, you can earn even more points and get on the fast track to elite status with elevated welcome offers on two Marriott Bonvoy® American Express® Cards. These offers end Sept. 30, 2026, so let's take a look at how to choose the right card for your travel style. A top-tier card with premium benefits The Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card is the most premium card in the lineup, offering benefits that enhance not only your Marriott stays but also your everyday life. New Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant cardholders can earn 150,000 bonus points and a $250 statement credit after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Offer ends Sept. 30. The Bonvoy Brilliant card has a $650 annual fee (see rates and fees), but when you combine the Bonvoy Brilliant's annual free night award (available upon annual card renewal, certain hotels have resort fees), which can be redeemed for up to 85,000 points per night at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels, and the annual $300 Brilliant Dining Credit (up to $25 in monthly statement credits for eligible dining purchases worldwide each calendar year), it's easy to get outsize value from the card before you even dip into the other benefits. Cardholders also get complimentary Marriott Bonvoy® Platinum Elite status, which includes benefits such as 50% bonus points on stays at participating brands, lounge access, room upgrades and late checkout. These benefits are subject to availability and apply only when a stay is booked at a qualifying rate at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels. You can earn up to a staggering 21 points per dollar spent on eligible purchases at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels on the card: 6 points for paying with the Bonvoy Brilliant card, up to 10 points for being a Marriott Bonvoy member and up to 5x points from Marriott Bonvoy on eligible hotel purchases with the 50% bonus points on stays benefit for Platinum Elite members. And with no foreign transaction fees (see rates and fees) and either a $120 statement credit for Global Entry or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck every four years, frequent travelers will reach for this card again and again. Whether you are a Marriott loyalist or only stay a few times each year, the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant card's complimentary Platinum Elite status, annual free night award (certain hotels have resort fees) and bonus points earning potential make it easy to take full advantage of its suite of benefits. And, if you apply by Sept. 30, you can earn 150,000 bonus points to use toward your next dream vacation. High earning potential for Marriott loyalists If you are looking for a lower annual fee or don't fancy yourself a frequent traveler, but still want to enjoy the benefits of elite status, the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card is a solid mid-tier option. The Bonvoy Bevy card has a $250 annual fee (see rates and fees), and new cardholders can earn 125,000 bonus points and a $150 statement credit after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Offer ends Sept. 30. Bonvoy Bevy cardholders get perks like a welcome gift of points when you stay at participating Marriott brands, automatic complimentary Marriott Bonvoy® Gold Elite status, complimentary room upgrades (subject to availability upon check-in) and a 2 p.m. late checkout (based on availability, when the stay is booked with a qualifying rate at hotels that participate in Marriott Bonvoy). You can also earn up to 18.5 Marriott Bonvoy points for every $1 spent on eligible purchases at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels: 6 points for paying with the Bonvoy Bevy card, up to 10 points for being a Marriott Bonvoy member and up to 2.5 points with the 25% Bonus Points on Stays benefit for Gold Elite members. When you combine the bonus points you can earn on stays, plus the Bonvoy Bevy's 125,000-point welcome offer, you'll be on your way to points-fueled vacations in no time. Bottom line No matter which card you choose, it's clear that a Marriott Bonvoy American Express card is the upgrade your next trip needs. Learn more about the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant American Express Card and the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy American Express Card before these elevated offers end on Sept. 30. Learn more about the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card and Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card. For rates and fees of the American Express Bonvoy Brilliant, click here. For rates and fees of the American Express Bonvoy Bevy, click here. Terms apply to all offer and benefit mentions.

item.title: Which AAdvantage card is right for you? Here are 3 options you should consider
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.17
Which AAdvantage card is right for you? Here are 3 options you should consider Editor's Note If you're considering a cobranded card with American Airlines, it's important to pick the right option for you. Each choice offers a different annual fee, its own set of perks and distinct earning rates. Among Citi's five AAdvantage cards, you may be struggling to decide which is the best for you. Here are my thoughts on which of the three most popular AAdvantage cards is the right fit for you, depending on how dedicated you are to American Airlines and how frequently you travel. Citi / AAdvantage credit cards: Key details Before diving deeper into each card individually, let's go through a quick refresher of their basic details. | Card | Welcome offer | Standout benefit | Annual fee | |---|---|---|---| | | Earn 50,000 bonus miles after spending $2,500 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. | | $0 introductory annual fee, then $99 | | | Earn 60,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. | | $350 | | | For a limited time, earn 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. | | $695 | The information for the Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Platinum Select: For those who fly AA occasionally If you only fly AA a couple of times each year, I recommend the AAdvantage Platinum Select. Its $0 introductory annual fee for the first year (then $99) means you can test having a cobranded card in your wallet without committing to an annual fee up front. While you won't get any lounge passes or statement credits with merchants, you may not need the Platinum Select to play that role if you already hold a premium travel rewards card. That doesn't mean the Platinum Select slacks on perks, though. You'll get your first checked bag free on domestic American Airlines flights, saving you at least $45 each way. Plus, you'll receive priority boarding on all American Airlines flights. More often than not, I find passengers on my flights are forced to check their carry-ons after the plane runs out of overhead space. With priority boarding, the odds of that happening to you are lower. And unlike some other cobranded cards, you don't need to book your flight with your Platinum Select card to enjoy these perks. To learn more, check out our full review of the AAdvantage Platinum Select. Globe: For those who fly AA often If you fly with American Airlines at least once a quarter but aren't a fully committed loyalist, the AAdvantage Globe is a solid choice. While it comes with a $350 price tag, it offers a roster of perks to offset the cost. Some of these benefits are four annual Admirals Club passes, up to $100 back as statement credits for inflight purchases, up to $100 Splurge statement credit for eligible brands (exclusions apply) and a companion certificate for eligible flights after each account anniversary (worth $99 plus taxes and fees). If you're able to use the companion certificate each year and take advantage of the lounge passes, you should get outsize value out of your annual fee without even having to touch the card's statement credits. That said, if you only fly with American a couple of times each year, you may have to put in more effort than it's worth to get sufficient value out of the Globe. In that case, I recommend considering a general travel rewards card instead. To learn more, check out our full review of the AAdvantage Globe. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Globe Executive: For those very loyal to AA As AAdvantage's top-tier credit card, the AAdvantage Executive is oriented toward those who fly American Airlines exclusively or very frequently. And it carries an annual fee to match: $695. Given that this annual fee is as high as it is, it requires careful consideration to ensure it fits your budget. While the Globe offers four Admirals Club passes each year, the Executive offers an Admirals Club membership. Given that a full Admirals Club membership costs a whopping up to $1,400 for new members, if you visit an Admirals Club several times a year, this benefit alone makes the annual fee worth it. While an Admirals Club membership is this card's standout benefit, it also offers travel credits, hotel and car rental elite status, and priority AA travel perks to help justify its annual fee. It's also worth noting that if you fly Alaska Airlines frequently in addition to AA, this card can be a great fit for you. To learn more, check out our full review of the AAdvantage Executive. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive Is it worth having multiple AAdvantage cards? The main appeal of an AAdvantage card is access to American Airlines–specific perks, such as priority boarding, a free checked bag and, on premium cards, Admirals Club access. For most travelers, one well-chosen AAdvantage card is enough to unlock meaningful value. That's especially true if you're not trying to stack statement credits, chase multiple welcome bonuses or fully commit to the AAdvantage ecosystem. Instead of holding multiple AAdvantage cards, many travelers will get more flexibility by pairing the AAdvantage card that best fits their travel habits with a premium travel rewards card. A premium card can complement your AA perks with broader lounge access, transferable rewards and additional statement credits. That said, if you do want to build out a wallet with more than one AAdvantage card, it's important to keep Citi's welcome bonus eligibility rules in mind so you're able to secure the strongest offers available. Alternatively, you could look at a Citi Strata card to earn flexible ThankYou Rewards points that can be transferred to a variety of airline partners, giving you more options beyond AA. Bottom line AAdvantage is one of the most popular airline loyalty programs, and it's a favorite among many of my colleagues here at TPG. If you're considering a Citi / AAdvantage card, you'll find several strong options designed to suit different types of American Airlines flyers. When choosing the right card, it's important to think realistically about how often you fly American Airlines and whether you're comfortable prioritizing AA over other carriers. It's also worth considering how frequently you travel through airports with Admirals Club locations, as lounge access can dramatically affect the overall value of certain cards. Pick the AAdvantage card that aligns with your travel habits, and you'll unlock perks that can meaningfully improve your experience — from smoother boarding to valuable savings and, in some cases, comfortable lounge access along the way. Related: How to choose an airline credit card

item.title: Aeroplan card's best-ever offer: Earn up to 115,000 bonus points
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.02
Aeroplan card's best-ever offer: Earn up to 115,000 bonus points Editor's Note The Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card (see rates and fees) recently underwent a major refresh, adding several valuable travel perks while increasing its annual fee from $95 to $195. New and existing cardmembers now receive automatic Aeroplan 25K status with no spending requirement, 15% savings on eligible Air Canada award flights and up to $100 in annual Air Canada statement credits. For a limited time, new cardmembers can also earn up to 115,000 bonus Aeroplan points: 75,000 bonus points after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening, plus an additional 40,000 bonus points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first 12 months from account opening. Here's what to know about the card's best-ever offer. Aeroplan card welcome offer The $195-per-year Aeroplan card is currently offering new cardholders its best-ever welcome offer. New cardholders can earn up to 115,000 bonus Aeroplan points: 75,000 bonus Aeroplan points after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening, plus an additional 40,000 bonus Aeroplan points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first 12 months from account opening. TPG's September 2026 valuations place Aeroplan points at 1.5 cents apiece, making this welcome offer worth $1,725. However, earning the full bonus requires $20,000 in spending during the first year, so before applying, consider whether that spending requirement fits naturally into your budget. Keep in mind that this card is affected by Chase's 5/24 rule, which means you will likely not be approved if you have opened five or more personal cards in the past 24 months, regardless of which issuer they're from. If you are eligible, check out our ideas for quickly meeting a minimum spending requirement, including prepaying insurance, rent or taxes to earn the entire welcome offer. Related: Air Canada's Aeroplan program: The ultimate guide to earning and redeeming points Aeroplan card earning rates Beyond its welcome offer, the Aeroplan card earns bonus points across several travel and everyday spending categories: - UPDATED: Up to 5 points per dollar spent on eligible Air Canada purchases — 3 points from the card plus 2 additional points from Air Canada when traveling as an Aeroplan 25K member - NEW: 3 points per dollar on travel purchases other than Air Canada - 3 points per dollar spent at grocery stores and dining (through Dec. 31, 2026; these categories will earn 2 points per dollar starting Jan. 1, 2027) - UPDATED: 2 points per dollar on gas station purchases - 1 point per dollar spent on other purchases The addition of 3 points per dollar on general travel is particularly useful, but the card will become less rewarding for dining and grocery purchases when those categories drop from 3 points per dollar to 2 points per dollar in 2027. Related: Maximizing credit cards to become points-rich without spending a ton Aeroplan card key benefits Beyond the points that you can earn, the Aeroplan card also offers several benefits that can be particularly valuable for frequent Air Canada travelers: - Automatic Aeroplan 25K elite status with no spending requirement, and all the benefits that come with this status - 15% savings on eligible flights booked with Aeroplan points - Up to $100 in annual Air Canada statement credits, split into two up to $50 semiannual credits - First free checked bag for cardmembers and up to eight travel companions traveling on the same reservation (travel must originate on an Air Canada flight) - No foreign transaction fees - Travel protections, such as auto rental insurance, baggage delay insurance, roadside assistance, trip cancellation and interruption insurance and trip delay reimbursement - Up to $120 statement credit for a Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or Nexus application every four years The card's Air Canada statement credits can help offset the $195 annual fee, while the 15% award discount can provide additional value for cardmembers who regularly redeem Aeroplan points for eligible itineraries that include Air Canada flights. Additionally, cardholders can continue to earn a 500-point bonus for every $2,000 spent on the card per calendar month, up to 1,500 bonus points per month, through Dec. 31, 2026. This benefit will be discontinued starting Jan. 1, 2027. Related: Credit card perks and benefits you should be using this month Bottom line The refreshed Aeroplan card is a strong option for frequent Air Canada travelers, especially with automatic 25K status, 15% savings on eligible award flights and up to $100 in annual Air Canada statement credits. The $195 annual fee is a big jump from the previous $95, but the current best-ever welcome offer of up to 115,000 points sweetens the deal. Aeroplan points can unlock flights on Air Canada and its extensive network of airline partners, including United Airlines. If you already have a use in mind for Aeroplan points and can comfortably meet the $20,000 spending requirement for the full bonus, now could be a good time to apply. To learn more, read our full review of the Aeroplan card. Apply here: Aeroplan card
